Second, learned counsel submits WAPDA maintains its own service framework and that it is a settled internal policy the Fundamental Rules and other general service laws apply only in areas not otherwise covered by the rules or instructions by the Authority itself. Reliance in this regard is placed on its Resolution No. 396 dated 07.06.1978, wherein it was resolved: in all matters not covered by the Rules framed by the Authority, or where the Rules are silent, the Fundamental Rules or Supplementary Rules framed by Federal Government shall be applicable. (I)/2022 20.05.2022 (the “2022 SRO’), whereby, through amendment, the proviso to sub-rule (1) of Rule 17 of Rules has been omitted with immediate effect. (I)/2022 has no adverse effect claim of the respondents, which had been initiated, processed, subjected to departmental rejection prior to 20.05.2022, and was therefore rightly adjudicated by the Federal Service Tribunal the unamended FR 17(1). paragraphs.text: Yahya Afridi, CJ.- petitioner, Water Power Development Authority (“WAPDA” or the “Authority”) has assailed the judgment 11.09.2024 rendered by the Federal Service Tribunal, whereby the service appeal filed by the respondents was allowed and arrears of pay and allowances on account of pro forma promotion were granted. Factual Background:

The respondents are employees of WAPDA. Prior to the year 1992, ten power generation units at Tarbela were operational the administrative control of the Chief Engineer, Tarbela Power Station I (“TPS I”). In July 1992, four additional generating units commenced operation at Tarbela under the administrative control of a separate Chief Engineer designated as Tarbela Power Station (“TPS II”). Consequent thereto, the seniority of employees posted at TPS I and TPS II came to be maintained separately, selection grade and promotions were granted on the basis of such segregated seniority lists.

The maintenance of separate seniority lists led to a series of service disputes. In the first round of litigation, four employees challenged the segregation and sought promotion and selection grade on the basis of a combined seniority. The matter ultimately reached the Supreme Court, which remanded the case to the Federal Service Tribunal for fresh determination. Henceforth, a combined seniority list of employees of TPS I and TPS II was eventually prepared. This, however, gave rise to a second round of litigation concerning consequential service benefits flowing from the revised seniority. Federal Service Tribunal held all to 5784 of 2024 :3: concerned employees were entitled to service benefits, including selection grade promotion, strictly in accordance with the combined seniority so determined.

In implementation said determinations, respondents were granted retrospective pro forma promotion account of refixation of seniority. Thereafter, through a formal application dated 05.01.2022, they sought payment of arrears of pay and allowances attached to the higher post in terms of FR 17(1). The said claim was declined by WAPDA vide order 02.03.2022 basis of Office Memo No. AD (EIB)07012/24021980 13.04.1987 (the “Office Memorandum”), in consultation with the Ministry of Water and Power under 18 of the WAPDA Act, 1958 (the “WAPDA Act”), which denies arrears for the retrospective period in the following terms: The question as to whether the employees who are granted proforma promotion from retrospective date in consequence re-fixation of seniority, are also entitled pay of the higher post, was under consideration for some time past. The Authority has now decided, in consultation with the Ministry of Water & Power, Government of Pakistan, that the concerned employees will be entitled to benefit of re-fixation of pay on account revision of seniority by the competent authority from a back date but would not be entitled to arrears of pay and allowances of the higher post. (emphasis provided)

(emphasis provided) A plain reading of the above extract leaves no manner of doubt that 18 of the WAPDA Act does not contemplate the framing statutory service rules. The Supreme Court expressly held that the provision merely empowers the Authority to prescribe procedures relating to appointment, terms conditions of service, disciplinary control, without requiring governmental approval and without conferring statutory force on such prescriptions. judgment further makes it abundantly clear that the source of power which an instrument is issued is determinative of its legal character. As held by Supreme Court, neither form nor nomenclature of an instrument is decisive. Unless it is framed under section 29 of the WAPDA Act, with the approval of the Government, it cannot attain statutory status. The distinction drawn by the Supreme Court between 18 and 29 is central. Whereas Section 18 authorizes internal governance, Section 29 alone provides mechanism for framing regulations having statutory force. Instruments were, therefore, categorically held to be administrative in nature. CPLAs No.5750 to 5784 of 2024 “12% 23. Itis not disputed the Office Memorandum was issued by invoking 18 of the WAPDA Act. It is also not the case of the petitioner it was framed as a regulation Section 29, approved by the Federal Government, or notified as subordinate legislation. The fact Office Memorandum was consultation with, or pursuant to the views of, the Ministry of Water Power does not alter its character. As is evident from the reasoning of the Supreme Court in Jamil Ahmed case (supra), mere consultation cannot substitute statutory requirement Government approval under Section 29, nor can it confer statutory force upon an administrative instruction. 24. petitioner’s reliance Resolution No. 07.06.1978 Office Memorandum 16.03.2006, also does not assist its case. At best, these instruments can at best regulate internal administration. They cannot, by their own force, override Statutory service rules or exclude application Rules. Indeed, Resolution No. 396 itself recognizes that the Fundamental Rules shall apply in matters not covered by rules framed by the Authority. It is by now settled that, instruments framed 29 can qualify as statutory rules, while instructions 18, being administrative, are devoid of necessary statutory force. 25.
